prompt: Don't use any tools and don't change any files. Write about 150 words about rivers, in 2 paragraphs.

text: I should just start writing rather than overthinking it further.

Rivers are some of the oldest storytellers on Earth. They start as snowmelt, springs, or rain gathering in high places, and they follow gravity toward the sea. Over thousands of years they carve canyons, build floodplains, and leave rich sediment behind, turning dry land into fertile ground. The Nile, the Amazon, and the Yangtze have each shaped whole landscapes. They've also shaped the civilizations that grew up along their banks and depended on their steady flow and their seasonal floods.

A river is also a living system. Fish migrate upstream to spawn, birds feed in the shallows, and forests line the banks, their roots holding the soil in place. People have always gathered near rivers for water, food, trade, and travel. Today many rivers face pollution, damming, and overuse, but restoration efforts show that they can recover when given the chance. Standing beside moving water reminds us that change is constant and that everything is connected.
